fields.description: The customer's email address, used to send order receipts and account notices.

A short alphanumeric loyalty tier code such as GOLD-1, SILVER-2 or BRONZE-3, assigned when the customer enrolls in the rewards program. Despite the column's name, this field has never stored the account's own numeric identifier.

An internal flag used only by the nightly batch job that reconciles this table against a separate internal system; it is not an attribute of the customer or the order, and carries no meaning once the export leaves that job.
The internal numeric identifier assigned to the customer account when it was first created.

This column has been used inconsistently by different store locations: in about half of exports it holds the shipping country for the order, and in the other half it holds the customer's loyalty-program tier name instead; the export itself does not say which convention a given row follows.
The stock-keeping unit code identifying the exact product variant most recently viewed by the customer on the storefront, logged for abandoned-cart follow-up.
The total monetary amount charged for the order, formatted as a decimal string with two places after the point.
The calendar date the order was placed by the customer.
Whether the customer asked for the order to be wrapped and marked as a gift at checkout.
The stock-keeping unit code identifying the exact product variant ordered.
The two-letter country code the parcel will be shipped to.

A duplicate column some orders carry from an old checkout form that also recorded the shipping country in free text; this export keeps both columns side by side for orders created before the main field was added.
The customer's named loyalty-program tier, such as Gold, Silver or Bronze.
The three-letter ISO country code the parcel will be shipped to, stored as free text; the legacy ledger named this column after an older, unrelated billing feature that was removed years ago.
Whether the customer asked for the order to be wrapped and marked as a gift at checkout, a column repurposed from an older membership-status flag of the same name.

A free-text reference code some regional offices write for their own internal paperwork; its meaning and format vary by region, and it is not read by any part of the customer or order record kept in the target schema.
The customer's email address, used for account contact and order receipts.
The internal numeric identifier assigned to the customer account.

A short alphanumeric loyalty tier code such as GOLD-1, SILVER-2 or BRONZE-3, assigned when the customer enrolls in the rewards program; despite its name, this column has never stored an account status flag.

An internal flag used only by the nightly reconciliation job against a separate internal system; it is not an attribute of the customer or the order, and carries no meaning once the export leaves that job.

The calendar date the order was placed by the customer.
The total monetary amount charged for the order, formatted as a decimal string with two places after the point.
The stock-keeping unit code identifying the exact product variant ordered.
Whether the customer asked for the order to be wrapped and marked as a gift at checkout.
The customer's named loyalty-program tier, such as Gold, Silver or Bronze.
The two-letter country code the parcel will be shipped to.

The three-letter ISO country code the parcel will be shipped to, stored as free text; the legacy ledger named this column after an older, unrelated billing feature that was removed years ago.
Whether the customer asked for the order to be wrapped and marked as a gift at checkout, a column repurposed from an older enrollment-status flag of the same name.
A free-text label naming which marketing channel or campaign referred the customer to sign up; it has no counterpart in the target order or customer schema.
The stock-keeping unit code identifying the exact product variant ordered, recorded as a secondary copy by an older point-of-sale terminal still in use at two stores.

A short free-text note support agents attach to a customer record for their own follow-up; it is not read by any other system and has no corresponding column in the target schema.
